quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ you arrive before noon, the hotel will hold your room without an extra charge.
quests.sentence: ____ you arrive before noon, the hotel will hold your room without an extra charge.
quests.hint: This is a possible situation, not something guaranteed to happen.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces this uncertain condition about your arrival time. 'When' would incorrectly suggest arriving before noon is already a sure thing.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the seasons change, the store rotates its window displays to match.
quests.sentence: ____ the seasons change, the store rotates its window displays to match.
quests.hint: The seasons changing is a certain, recurring event, not something in doubt.
quests.explanation: 'When' fits this certain, routine cycle. 'If' would incorrectly suggest there's doubt about whether the seasons will change.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The construction crew will keep working ____ the bridge is fully reopened to traffic.
quests.sentence: The construction crew will keep working ____ the bridge is fully reopened to traffic.
quests.hint: The work continues right up to that point, not simply at a single moment.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows the ongoing work stops exactly when the bridge reopens. 'When' would only mark a single moment, missing the sense of continuing duration.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the storm actually reaches the coast, residents are advised to stock up on supplies now.
quests.sentence: ____ the storm actually reaches the coast, residents are advised to stock up on supplies now.
quests.hint: Forecasts are never certain - this describes a possibility, not something guaranteed.
quests.explanation: 'If' captures the genuine uncertainty about whether the storm will actually reach the coast. 'When' would incorrectly suggest this is already a sure thing.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the tide comes in each evening, the fishing boats return to the harbor.
quests.sentence: ____ the tide comes in each evening, the fishing boats return to the harbor.
quests.hint: The tide coming in every evening is a predictable, certain event.
quests.explanation: 'When' fits this reliable, recurring natural pattern. 'If' would incorrectly suggest doubt about whether the tide will come in.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ Sam gets the promotion, he's planning to take the whole team out to celebrate - though nothing is confirmed yet.
quests.sentence: ____ Sam gets the promotion, he's planning to take the whole team out to celebrate - though nothing is confirmed yet.
quests.hint: The phrase 'nothing is confirmed yet' tells you this isn't a sure thing.
quests.explanation: 'If' matches the explicit uncertainty mentioned. 'When' would wrongly suggest the promotion is already a certainty.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The overdue fine keeps increasing ____ you return the book.
quests.sentence: The overdue fine keeps increasing ____ you return the book.
quests.hint: The fine keeps growing continuously, right up to the moment of return - this is about duration, not a requirement.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows the fine increases continuously up to that point. 'Unless' would instead frame returning the book as a requirement to avoid a fine altogether, which isn't quite this ongoing-increase situation.
quests.grammarRule: Time vs Condition - until, not unless

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: You won't get your security deposit back ____ you leave the apartment in good condition.
quests.sentence: You won't get your security deposit back ____ you leave the apartment in good condition.
quests.hint: Getting the deposit back depends on a requirement being met, not simply on time passing.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the deposit is withheld specifically when the apartment isn't left in good condition. 'Until' would incorrectly suggest the deposit is just delayed rather than genuinely dependent on this condition.
quests.grammarRule: Condition vs Time - unless, not until

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The free trial continues ____ you decide to cancel it yourself.
quests.sentence: The free trial continues ____ you decide to cancel it yourself.
quests.hint: The trial keeps going continuously, right up to the moment you choose to stop it.
quests.explanation: 'Until' captures this ongoing continuation that ends only when you cancel. 'Unless' would instead frame cancellation as a requirement to prevent something, which doesn't match this simple duration.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ she finishes her final training hours, Priya can officially start practicing as a therapist.
quests.sentence: ____ she finishes her final training hours, Priya can officially start practicing as a therapist.
quests.hint: Finishing her training hours is essentially guaranteed to happen - it's a matter of when, not whether.
quests.explanation: 'Once' shows that completing her training directly triggers the next step. 'When' would also describe this reasonably well, but 'if' would incorrectly suggest doubt about whether she'll finish, when really it's just a matter of time.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the pilot program succeeds, the company plans to roll it out nationwide next year.
quests.sentence: ____ the pilot program succeeds, the company plans to roll it out nationwide next year.
quests.hint: Success here is genuinely uncertain - this isn't a guaranteed outcome.
quests.explanation: 'If' captures the real uncertainty about whether the pilot program will succeed. 'Once' would incorrectly suggest success is already assured and just a matter of timing.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the permits are approved, construction can begin immediately - it's really just a matter of paperwork at this point.
quests.sentence: ____ the permits are approved, construction can begin immediately - it's really just a matter of paperwork at this point.
quests.hint: The phrase 'just a matter of paperwork' tells you approval is basically assured - this is about timing, not real doubt.
quests.explanation: 'Once' fits this near-certain situation, where approval is expected and construction is triggered by its completion. 'When' would also work reasonably here, but 'if' would incorrectly suggest genuine doubt about whether the permits will be approved.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: Wash your hands thoroughly ____ you start preparing the meal.
quests.sentence: Wash your hands thoroughly ____ you start preparing the meal.
quests.hint: This is simply about the order of two steps, not a condition or possibility.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows the hand-washing happens earlier in a fixed sequence of steps. 'If' would incorrectly turn this into a conditional possibility rather than a straightforward instruction.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the client approves the final draft, we can move forward with printing.
quests.sentence: ____ the client approves the final draft, we can move forward with printing.
quests.hint: Approval isn't guaranteed here - this describes a real possibility, not just a sequence of steps.
quests.explanation: 'If' captures the genuine uncertainty about whether the client will approve. 'Before' or 'after' would only describe timing, missing this sense of a real condition that might not be met.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The refund will be processed automatically ____ the airline receives your cancellation request.
quests.sentence: The refund will be processed automatically ____ the airline receives your cancellation request.
quests.hint: This describes a reliable next step triggered by receiving the request, not a real possibility that might not happen.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows the refund reliably follows receipt of the request, as a simple sequence. 'Unless' would incorrectly frame this as a requirement to prevent something, which isn't the relationship here.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The delivery driver couldn't find the address ____ the house numbers on the street were poorly marked.
quests.sentence: The delivery driver couldn't find the address ____ the house numbers on the street were poorly marked.
quests.hint: This explains the actual reason for the trouble, not a possibility or a moment in time.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for the driver's difficulty. 'When' would only mark timing, missing the explanation of why it happened.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ passengers could board more quickly, the airline introduced a new priority lane at security.
quests.sentence: ____ passengers could board more quickly, the airline introduced a new priority lane at security.
quests.hint: This new lane was created with a specific future goal in mind, not to explain something that already happened.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces this intentional purpose, with 'could' expressing the enabled benefit. 'Because' would incorrectly frame faster boarding as an existing reason rather than a goal.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The greenhouse plants will wilt within days ____ someone waters them regularly.
quests.sentence: The greenhouse plants will wilt within days ____ someone waters them regularly.
quests.hint: Wilting happens specifically when watering does NOT occur - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the wilting depends on watering failing to happen. 'If' would need 'doesn't water' added to express the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ ticket prices double, loyal fans say they'll still attend every home game.
quests.sentence: ____ ticket prices double, loyal fans say they'll still attend every home game.
quests.hint: Their attendance stays the same no matter what happens with prices - stronger than a simple condition.
quests.explanation: 'Even if' shows their commitment holds regardless of a possible price increase. 'Unless' would incorrectly suggest a price increase could actually stop them from attending.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The team will miss the playoffs ____ they win all three remaining games.
quests.sentence: The team will miss the playoffs ____ they win all three remaining games.
quests.hint: Missing the playoffs happens specifically when winning all three does NOT occur - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the outcome depends on failing to win all three games. 'Even if' would incorrectly suggest the outcome stays the same regardless of how many games they win, which isn't true here.
quests.grammarRule: Condition - unless (built-in negative) vs even if (regardless)

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ nobody else shows up to help, Marcus is determined to finish cleaning the park by himself.
quests.sentence: ____ nobody else shows up to help, Marcus is determined to finish cleaning the park by himself.
quests.hint: His determination holds true no matter how many people show up - or don't.
quests.explanation: 'Even if' emphasizes that his commitment doesn't depend on others' participation at all. 'Unless' would incorrectly suggest he'd stop if nobody showed up, which contradicts his determination.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the annual inspection is complete, the factory can resume full production.
quests.sentence: ____ the annual inspection is complete, the factory can resume full production.
quests.hint: Completing the inspection is the specific trigger for resuming production, not just a general point in time.
quests.explanation: 'Once' emphasizes that finishing the inspection directly triggers production resuming. 'When' could describe simple timing but doesn't capture this completion-triggers-next-step relationship as clearly.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The elevator will remain out of service ____ a licensed technician inspects it and signs off on the repair.
quests.sentence: The elevator will remain out of service ____ a licensed technician inspects it and signs off on the repair.
quests.hint: Being out of service happens specifically when this required inspection does NOT occur yet.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the service depends on this required inspection happening first. 'Before' would only describe timing, missing the sense of a genuine requirement that must be met.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: Interest continues to accumulate on the balance ____ the full amount is paid off.
quests.sentence: Interest continues to accumulate on the balance ____ the full amount is paid off.
quests.hint: The interest keeps building continuously, right up to the moment of full payment - this is about ongoing duration.
quests.explanation: 'Until' captures this continuous accumulation that stops exactly at full payment. 'Unless' would instead frame payment as a one-time requirement to avoid interest altogether, rather than describing this ongoing buildup.
quests.grammarRule: Time vs Condition - until, not unless

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the trail was steep and rocky the whole way up, the view from the summit made every step worth it.
quests.sentence: ____ the trail was steep and rocky the whole way up, the view from the summit made every step worth it.
quests.hint: The worthwhile view despite the difficult trail is the unexpected twist here.
quests.explanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the tough climb and the rewarding view. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest the difficulty was the reason the view was good.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The north side of the building gets very little natural light, ____ the south-facing rooms are bright all day.
quests.sentence: The north side of the building gets very little natural light, ____ the south-facing rooms are bright all day.
quests.hint: Two different sides of the building are simply being compared here, with neither happening despite the other.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting conditions. 'Although' would suggest one side is bright despite some obstacle, which isn't the relationship being described.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: Employees receive a small bonus ____ they complete five years with the company.
quests.sentence: Employees receive a small bonus ____ they complete five years with the company.
quests.hint: Reaching five years is a certain milestone that will eventually happen, not something in doubt.
quests.explanation: 'When' fits this certain, expected milestone. 'If' would incorrectly suggest doubt about whether employees will ever reach five years, when it's simply a matter of time.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the renovation stays on schedule despite the recent delays, the new wing should open to the public by early spring.
quests.sentence: ____ the renovation stays on schedule despite the recent delays, the new wing should open to the public by early spring.
quests.hint: The phrase 'despite the recent delays' signals real uncertainty about staying on schedule.
quests.explanation: 'If' captures the genuine uncertainty here, especially given the delays already mentioned. 'When' would incorrectly suggest staying on schedule is already a sure thing.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The community garden project will lose its city funding entirely ____ organizers submit a revised proposal within thirty days.
quests.sentence: The community garden project will lose its city funding entirely ____ organizers submit a revised proposal within thirty days.
quests.hint: Losing funding happens specifically when the revised proposal does NOT get submitted in time - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the funding loss depends on the proposal failing to be submitted in time. 'If' would need 'don't submit' added to express the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the final inspection report comes back clean, residents can begin moving back into the building after months away.
quests.sentence: ____ the final inspection report comes back clean, residents can begin moving back into the building after months away.
quests.hint: The clean report is the specific trigger that allows the next step, and it's expected to happen - this is about timing, not real doubt.
quests.explanation: 'Once' captures the idea that the clean report directly triggers residents moving back. 'If' would incorrectly suggest real doubt about whether the report will come back clean.
